questions.title: Where do you drop your ball if someone stops it on purpose?
questions.question: If your ball is rolling and a person (not on the green) stops it or knocks it away on purpose, where do you drop your ball?

choices.text: Where you hit your last shot from
Within 1 club-length of where your ball would have stopped
Where you last hit the ball

questions.explanation: You must drop your ball within 1 club-length of where you think your ball would have stopped if no one had touched it.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The length of your golf club. You can use your club to measure how far you are allowed to drop the ball from the spot.

questions.teachingTip: Let children use their own club to measure a club-length on the course, so they see how far that really is.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think you go back to where you hit the ball, but the correct place is near where the ball would have finished after rolling.

questions.title: Where to drop a ball intentionally deflected by a person
questions.question: If your ball in motion is intentionally stopped or deflected by a person (not on the green), where should you drop it?

choices.text: Within 1 club-length of where it would have come to rest
At the point where it was struck

questions.explanation: If your ball is intentionally stopped or deflected by a person (not on the green), you must drop a ball within 1 club-length of the estimated spot where it would have come to rest.
